hint.click-for-details: Click on a phoneme for details

consonants.diagram: Consonants organized by manner (rows: how the sound is made) and place (columns: where in the mouth). Within each cell: voiceless left, voiced right.

monophthongs.diagram: Vowels plotted by tongue position. Vertical axis shows tongue height (high to low). Horizontal axis shows tongue backness (front to back).

diphthongs.diagram: Vowels that glide between two positions. Each arrow traces the tongue's movement from start to end.

en.description: Pronunciations are obtained from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, which contains over 134,000 North American English words.

things-to-know.american-accent: Pronunciations reflect General American English, not British or other varieties
things-to-know.coverage: Some words may not be found, especially newer terms, slang, and proper nouns
things-to-know.multiple-variants: Words with multiple pronunciations (like 'read') show all variants

es.description: Pronunciations are generated using rule-based grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for Latin American Spanish (seseo, yeismo).

things-to-know.dialect: Pronunciations reflect Latin American Spanish, not Peninsular Spanish
things-to-know.rule-based: Transcription is rule-based and runs entirely in your browser, no dictionary lookup needed
things-to-know.stress: Stress is assigned automatically based on Spanish orthographic rules and accent marks

credits-page.title: Credits & Sources
credits-page.description: Phonaria uses open source projects, linguistic research, and freely licensed resources.

wikimedia.title: Phonetic Audio Samples
wikimedia.content: Phonetic audio samples come from the General phonetics gallery on Wikimedia Commons. The recordings were created by Wikimedia contributors and are used under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike and compatible licenses. See individual file pages for authorship and license details.

sagittal.title: Sagittal Illustrations
sagittal.content: Sagittal cross-section diagrams in the articulation panels are adapted from illustrations by Tavin and Nardog on Wikimedia Commons. The original artwork was modified to create consistent variants for each phoneme.

example-audio.title: Example Word Audio
example-audio.content: Example word recordings in phoneme details are AI-generated. Synthetic audio lets us iterate on the word list without re-recording. When the set stabilizes, we plan to replace these with human recordings.

cmu.title: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary
cmu.content: Transcription uses the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary from Carnegie Mellon University. The dictionary contains over 134,000 North American English words with phonetic transcriptions and is released under a BSD license.

wordfreq.title: wordfreq Word Frequency Data
wordfreq.content: Curated word lists for client-side lookup are generated using wordfreq by Robyn Speer. The library combines frequency data from Google Books Ngrams, OpenSubtitles, SUBTLEX, Wikipedia, and other corpora. Data is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

free-dictionary.title: Free Dictionary API
free-dictionary.content: Dictionary definitions come from the Free Dictionary API using Wiktionary data. Content is licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0. Audio files cite Wikimedia Commons with per-file licenses.

phonetic-data.title: Phonetic Data
phonetic-data.content: Articulatory descriptions, phoneme features, and IPA classifications draw from standard phonetic references and linguistics research.
